title: Concurrency Control: Pessimistic vs Optimistic Locking in Flash Sales

steps.prompt: During high-concurrency checkout, multiple orders query the same Product inventory row simultaneously. Which pattern prevents race condition overselling without holding prolonged exclusive database locks?

options.label: Optimistic Concurrency Control with a Version timestamp validated at DML commit and client retry
options.rationale: Optimistic concurrency avoids holding prolonged database locks during payment authorization, validating version consistency at the instant of commit.

options.label: Pessimistic locking using SOQL FOR UPDATE acquired prior to third-party payment authorization
options.distractorAntipattern: Holding database locks across external HTTP callouts causes severe lock wait timeouts across concurrent buyers.
options.rationale: Holding pessimistic locks while waiting for 3rd-party payment gateway callouts freezes database rows for all users and causes lock timeouts.

options.label: Platform Cache storage of inventory counts with scheduled asynchronous reconciliation to database
options.distractorAntipattern: In-memory cache without transactional row locking leads to dirty reads and severe overselling during traffic spikes.
options.rationale: Platform Cache provides fast reads but lacks transactional ACID isolation, leading to dirty reads and oversold inventory under high checkout concurrency.
